note: He passes the first two criteria cleanly. He is a tech entrepreneur and small business owner with a home gym and children at college, and health is unambiguously the neglected domain — he said so himself in the ICP's own terms: 'priority has been business, kids, and so forth. And I've kind of achieved that... your new startup should be your body, not a new idea.' The three misses are decisive. On income he named a range an order of magnitude below the offer. On starting point he is roughly 60-70 lb above a healthy weight at 118 kg and 5'11", with sleep apnea and a deteriorating back, which is rescue rather than good-to-great. And not_deconditioned is the clearest failure of that criterion anywhere in this batch — the ICP explicitly excludes people who are 50 lb overweight and gym-averse, and this prospect is both, saying of the weights in his own basement 'every time I try, I feel stressed... whenever I do lift weights, I just don't feel better. I feel worse. I feel angry.' He was nonetheless taken through a full twenty-five-minute closing call. The useful observation is that the exclusion criterion did its job as a description and had no effect as a filter: nothing in the setting process or the script surfaced weight, conditioning or price expectation before a closer's time was spent.
